reason: The executor task combines pre-mutation validation with failure recovery, which are independently reviewable work units with a composition boundary.
trigger_signals: Composition requires an explicit joint audit

evidence.claim: TASK-201 has separate invalid-input and partial-failure acceptance criteria.

preserved_parent.title: Implement safe executor
preserved_parent.summary: Execute validated plans and recover from partial failure.

acceptance_criteria.description: Invalid plans are rejected before mutation.

required_evidence.description: Valid, invalid, and partial-failure tests pass.

nodes.title: Implement pre-mutation validation
nodes.summary: Reject invalid operation plans before any mutable action begins.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every invalid plan case is rejected before mutation.

required_evidence.description: Invalid-plan tests prove that mutation never starts.

nodes.title: Implement recoverable execution
nodes.summary: Execute valid plans and return recoverable state after partial failure.

acceptance_criteria.description: Partial failures expose enough state for deterministic recovery.

nodes.title: Audit safe executor composition
nodes.summary: Verify validation and recovery compose into the preserved executor contract.

acceptance_criteria.description: Validation, execution, failure, and recovery scenarios pass together.

dependency_mapping.rationale: Both implementation branches consume the verified executor contract.

user_decisions.question: Should validation and recovery be independently reviewable branches?
user_decisions.answer: Yes; preserve the parent contract and require a joint integration audit.

impact.scope: No external scope change; TASK-201 becomes a stable work-package with two implementation children.
impact.risk: Adds coordination overhead but isolates validation and recovery failures.
impact.execution_order: Validation precedes recovery implementation; the joint audit follows both.
